subject: AcmeHealth latency incident — SRE briefing, action items, and OKR impacts
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Haines <tom.h@aurelia.com>, John Miller <jm@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SRE postmortem — AcmeHealth latency incident (Feb 17)

Folks — opening this thread with the postmortem summary and proposed actions for QBR/Ops leadership. Short summary first, details below.

One-line summary: On 2026-02-17 14:03 UTC, a runtime memory compaction triggered a cascade of KV cache evictions for quantized model variants serving AcmeHealth, producing sustained token-generation latency spikes and an SLA breach for one Dedicated cluster. Incident lasted ~2h17m; SLA window breached for ~1h05m for the affected customer.

Impact:
- Affected: 1 Dedicated pool (us-west-2), ~12 p95 requests/minute routed to that pool; primary customer: AcmeHealth (production).
- Symptom: p95 token latency from ~120ms -> 5–8s; transient 503s on small subset of requests while pools recycled.
- SLA: Missed 99.9% p95 target for the rolling hour (calculated per contract).

Root cause (short): An automated GPU memory compaction process interacted poorly with our new quantized model kernel in 2026-02-16 deploy. Compaction caused aggressive KV cache trimming; it exposed a latent race in cache eviction that caused repeated cache misses at warmup and blocked task scheduling, producing queuing and OOM restarts in a subset of workers.

Immediate remediation performed (Feb 17):
- Disabled scheduled compaction and rolled back the kernel flags to last-known-good (14:50 UTC).
- Redeployed affected pool with warmed caches (15:05 UTC).
- Temporarily rate-limited long-seq generation from AcmeHealth routes until warm caches stabilized (15:20–16:20 UTC).

Attachments: the full postmortem PDF and a one-sheet SLA impact spreadsheet attached. Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b-postmortem-acme

Open actions I recommend we track (high level):
1) Patch: fix race in cache eviction + add deterministic backoff for compaction. (Owner: @karthik_iyer) — ETA 2026-02-22. Jira INF-4821.
2) SLA remediation: propose credit calculation and customer messaging for AcmeHealth. (Owner: @rachel_kim / Finance & CS) — ETA 2026-02-20.
3) QBR one-pager: impact summary, technical root cause, mitigation plan, and proposed runbook changes. (Owner: @marissa_cole) — ETA 2026-02-19.
4) Dedicated pool policy: add circuit-breaker and automatic fallback to compatible model variant to avoid full pool recycle on future kernel regressions. (Owner: Platform Reliability) — ETA TBD.

Please review, add owners/edits inline, and let me know if we should surface a formal credit to AcmeHealth or start with a goodwill commitment + technical readout.

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Sr. Manager, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference

Thanks, Irene — good concise summary. A few asks from exec side before we deliver anything to the customer / QBR pack: 

- Can you convert the "Open actions" into a single-page tracker with explicit acceptance criteria for each item? Execs want: what success looks like and how we'll validate it.
- Important: quantify how this affects our OKRs for Reliability and Customer Trust (e.g., expected p95 improvement post-patch, SLA runway / risk to other Dedicated customers). Put numbers where possible.
- For the SLA credit ask: propose a single line we can present to AcmeHealth; include the financial estimate and whether this requires legal sign-off. Rachel, can you lead that calc?
- Please make sure the patch Jira is P0 and include a rollback plan for the patch itself.

Marissa — please own the QBR one-pager and include a short "what we changed in platform policy" blurb. Karthik — can you confirm patch ETA and whether we need an emergency deploy window?

I'll be joining the QBR prep sync on Friday to review the one-pager.

Vivek

Customer comms: John, Tom — we propose a 1:1 technical readout + proposed credit. We should schedule a 30m call early next week; John, are you available Mon/Tue? I can lead the readout and present the fix plan.
